title: Backdoor Purification for LoRA-Tuned LLMs via Null-Space Projection
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 30 Sep 2026]
    Title:Backdoor Purification for LoRA-Tuned LLMs via Null-Space Projection
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:With the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, the risk of backdoor attacks has become more severe. Existing backdoor purification methods typically rely on at least one of the strong assumptions, such as prior knowledge of triggers, access to clean references, or aggressive retraining, and they often lack comprehensive evaluations. These constraints substantially limit their practical applicability. To overcome these challenges, our work proposes purifying LoRA-tuned LLMs without these assumptions and even without post-hoc retraining of the suspect parameters. Our objective is to significantly reduce the attack success rates (ASR) while preserving both (i) the base model's general capabilities and (ii) the new downstream skills learned through the adapter. Through a series of ablation studies, we progressively scale our approach from a single layer in a text classification setting to a full-parameter LLM in the generative task. Through careful data curation and feature approximation, we extract high-fidelity backdoor directions and, for each layer or head, construct orthogonal null spaces in both the input and output channels, onto which the LoRA updates are projected. Empirically, our null-space projection method reduces the ASR from nearly 100% to less than 10%, while preserving the base model's benign performance and the adapter's learned abilities during downstream task adaptation.

report.summary: A new method purifies LoRA-tuned LLMs of backdoors by projecting adapter updates into null spaces, cutting attack success from nearly 100% to under 10%.
report.background: Large language models are increasingly customized through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, especially LoRA, which lets developers train small adapter weights instead of full models. This has spawned a vibrant ecosystem of shareable adapters on model hubs, but also a supply-chain risk: poisoned fine-tuning data can implant backdoors so a hidden trigger makes the model behave maliciously. Existing defenses often assume prior knowledge of triggers, access to clean reference models, or costly retraining, making them impractical for real-world third-party adapters. This paper tackles that gap by purifying LoRA-tuned LLMs without those assumptions and without post-hoc retraining of suspect parameters. It extracts backdoor directions and projects LoRA updates onto orthogonal null spaces, aiming to remove malicious behavior while preserving both base-model generality and newly learned downstream skills. The work reflects growing concern over PEFT security and adapter-marketplace trust.
key_points: The method purifies LoRA-tuned LLMs without assuming trigger knowledge, clean reference models, or retraining. It extracts high-fidelity backdoor directions and constructs orthogonal null spaces in input and output channels, then projects LoRA updates onto those spaces to suppress malicious behavior while keeping benign adapter functionality.

The authors scale their approach from a single layer in text classification to a full-parameter LLM in generative tasks. Through ablation studies, careful data curation, and feature approximation, they show the technique can generalize beyond simple settings and handle realistic adapter-based fine-tuning scenarios.

Null-space projection operates per layer or attention head, targeting the channels where backdoor features flow. By making LoRA updates orthogonal to identified backdoor directions, the method reduces attack success rates from nearly 100% to less than 10% in experiments.

Crucially, purification preserves both the base model's general capabilities and the adapter's learned downstream skills. This balances safety and utility, addressing a common failure mode of aggressive defenses that degrade model quality or erase useful fine-tuning.

The work highlights a practical security gap in the LoRA ecosystem: shared adapters can carry hidden backdoors, and defenders often lack clean data or trigger details. The proposed purification offers a post-hoc, retraining-free pathway for safer adapter deployment.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this research strengthens the case for adapter marketplaces and MLOps pipelines that scan, purify, and certify third-party LoRA weights before deployment. It could become part of model supply-chain security, alongside provenance and vulnerability scanning. For developers, it offers a potentially cheap post-hoc defense: sanitize suspect adapters without retraining or clean reference data, preserving downstream skills. That lowers the cost of safely using community fine-tunes. For regular users, it means downloaded or hosted models may be less likely to hide trigger-activated harmful behavior. However, it is not a silver bullet: adaptive attacks, generative-task robustness, and false negatives need further evaluation before production reliance.
report.tools: Follow Hugging Face PEFT and Transformers for LoRA adapter workflows, plus Safetensors for safe weight handling. Security-focused projects worth watching include BackdoorLLM, Garak, LLM Guard, and NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails for red-teaming and runtime protection. Check the paper's arXiv page for code or artifact releases, and monitor BackdoorBench for related attack and defense benchmarks.
